topics.title: Document Anatomy & HTML5 Standards
topics.content:
# Document Anatomy & HTML5 Standards

This topic delivers a thorough exploration of the HTML document skeleton and the rationale behind each head-level construct. Correct document anatomy ensures predictable rendering across browsers and is the foundation for accessibility and SEO.

Why <!DOCTYPE html> matters
The <!DOCTYPE html> declaration tells browsers to render in standards mode. Omitting or mis-declaring it can cause legacy quirks mode rendering, leading to inconsistent box-model behavior.

Essential head elements:
- \`<meta charset="utf-8">\`: sets character encoding and prevents garbled text.
- \`<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">\`: enables responsive scaling on mobile.
- \`<title>\`: critical for user context and SEO.
- Links to resources: stylesheets and preloads.

Minimal example:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
  <title>My App</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <main id="app">
    <!-- app root -->
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

topics.title: CSS Syntax, Selectors, & The Cascade
topics.content:
# CSS Syntax, Selectors, & The Cascade

Deep mastery of CSS starts with selectors and the cascade. This topic covers selector types, specificity calculation, and practical strategies to avoid specificity conflicts in large codebases.

Selector categories and examples:
- Element selectors: \`div\`, \`p\` — low specificity
- Class selectors: \`.btn\`, \`.card\` — medium specificity
- ID selectors: \`#main-header\` — higher specificity
- Attribute selectors and pseudo-classes: \`[type="submit"]\`, \`:hover\` — medium specificity

Specificity rules (summary):
1. Count ID selectors
2. Count class/attribute/pseudo-class selectors
3. Count element/pseudo-element selectors
4. Later rules override earlier rules when specificity ties

Example:

```css
/* base */
.btn { padding: 8px 12px; }
/* component */
.btn--primary { background: blue; color: white; }
#hero .btn--primary { background: darkblue; }
```

topics.title: The CSS Box Model Masterclass
topics.content:
# The CSS Box Model Masterclass

The box model governs layout. This topic explains how content, padding, border, and margin are composed and how `box-sizing` influences measurements.

Two models:
- Content-box (default): width/height apply to content only.
- Border-box: width/height include padding and border — recommended for consistent sizing.

Practical rules:
```css
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
```

Example code:

```css
.card { box-sizing: border-box; width: 300px; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #ddd; }
```

topics.title: Deep Dive into Flexbox
topics.content:
# Deep Dive into Flexbox

Flexbox is designed for one-dimensional layouts. Learn container and item properties with practical examples for navbars, card rows, and equal height columns.

Core container properties:
- display: flex; flex-direction; justify-content; align-items; flex-wrap; gap;

Core item properties:
- flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis; order; align-self

Example — responsive row with equal-width items:
```css
.container { display: flex; gap: 12px; }
.item { flex: 1 1 200px; }
```

Key takeaways:
- Flexbox is ideal for small-scale layouts (navs, toolbars).
